Past-tense overregularization

Source: R/data.R
overregularization.Rd

Overregularization errors (goed, holded) out of all irregular past-tense contexts, for 24 children recorded every six months from 30 to 60 months. Errors are rare, and their rate stays about the same across ages while children differ in how often they make them. For binomial models of errors out of attempts and for testing an effect that is absent.

Usage

overregularization

Format

A tibble with 144 rows and 4 columns:

child

Child ID, C01 to C24.

age

Age in months.

attempts

Irregular past-tense contexts in the recording.

errors

Overregularizations among them.

Source

data-raw/overregularization.R

Details

True model, in log-odds: -3.2, with by-child intercepts of SD 0.5, so about 4% of attempts are errors. Age has no effect. Children attempt more irregular past tenses as they get older.

References

Marcus, G. F., Pinker, S., Ullman, M., Hollander, M., Rosen, T. J. & Xu, F. (1992). Overregularization in language acquisition. Monographs of the Society for Research in Child Development, 57(4). doi:10.2307/1166115

Examples

head(overregularization)
#> # A tibble: 6 × 4
#>   child   age attempts errors
#>   <fct> <int>    <int>  <int>
#> 1 C01      30       17      0
#> 2 C01      36       26      4
#> 3 C01      42       30      1
#> 4 C01      48       42      0
#> 5 C01      54       33      2
#> 6 C01      60       44      2
